title: Troubleshooting Siphonage and Gurgling Drains
description: Gurgling noises coming from a sink or bathtub fixture when draining often point to an inadequate or blocked vent line. When water travels through a drain line without proper airflow, it creates a atmospheric pressure differential (negative pressure vacuum) behind the water flow. This vacuum forces air to be pulled through nearby trap seals, siphoning out the protective water seal and allowing sewer gases into the living space. Inspecting roof vents for debris or testing for adequate venting helps identify whether an Air Admittance Valve (AAV) or roof stack restoration is needed per local building codes.

Troubleshooting Siphonage and Gurgling Drains

Gurgling noises coming from a sink or bathtub fixture when draining often point to an inadequate or blocked vent line. When water travels through a drain line without proper airflow, it creates a atmospheric pressure differential (negative pressure vacuum) behind the water flow. This vacuum forces air to be pulled through nearby trap seals, siphoning out the protective water seal and allowing sewer gases into the living space. Inspecting roof vents for debris or testing for adequate venting helps identify whether an Air Admittance Valve (AAV) or roof stack restoration is needed per local building codes.
